definition: Need for affect is a person’s tendency to orient toward the emotional or feeling-based aspects of information and messages. In persuasion research, people higher in need for affect are more likely to be influenced by the emotional tone or valence of a message.

reasons: The packet does not explicitly define “need for affect” as a general “tendency to orient toward the emotional or feeling-based aspects of information and messages.” It only refers to participants’ “Need for Affect (NFA) orientation” in relation to matching with affective message contents.

Although the packet supports that message effectiveness/attitudes can depend on the match between message valence (affective content) and individuals’ NFA orientation, it does not explicitly justify the specific wording that higher NFA are “more likely to be influenced by the emotional tone or valence of a message” as a general definitional claim.

Because the definition’s core characterization (“tendency to orient toward emotional/feeling-based aspects”) is not directly supported by the provided packet text, the definition is not defensibly supported in full.
